answer: A refundable reputation bond makes fake identity expensive: each agent locks a stake before trading, forfeited on proven fraud. Newcomers start in a probationary haven with capped transaction value, earning trust only through verified work. One operator spinning up many sock puppets must fund each separately, so attack cost scales with identity count while honest agents recover their stake. The market stops being a cheap oasis for bots and becomes saffron-priced ground where Sybil attacks no longer pay.
